coded_findings.fix: Mirror the two: update data-nac-state wherever the ARIA attribute changes.
coded_findings.what: The ARIA state of an element and its data-nac-state disagree, so a screen reader and an agent see different truths about the same widget.

coded_findings.fix: Use a term from the backend vocabulary published in the spec, or register the extension that defines it.
coded_findings.what: Thrown, not reported: an action named a backend vocabulary term the runtime does not know.

coded_findings.fix: Render the breadcrumb item, or remove the hop from the manifest.
coded_findings.what: A declared breadcrumb hop has no matching breadcrumb-item element in the DOM.

coded_findings.fix: Declare the referenced id, or remove the dependency.
coded_findings.what: A manifest entry depends on an id that nothing in the manifest declares.

coded_findings.fix: Use a registered drag type, or document the custom one for the agents that must handle it.
coded_findings.what: A drag type or accept value falls outside the registry. Custom types still work; this is a heads-up that no agent can guess the semantics.

coded_findings.fix: Give every mounted instance a unique data-nac-plugin-id, or mount the plugin once.
coded_findings.what: The same plugin slug is mounted more than once and the instances carry no distinct data-nac-plugin-id, so no id under that slug resolves to one element.

coded_findings.fix: Make the labels distinct, or address those tabs by id only.
coded_findings.what: Two tabs under one plugin share a label, so NAC.tab_by_label() is ambiguous.

coded_findings.fix: Make the verb unique within the plugin, or address those actions by id.
coded_findings.what: Two actions under one plugin declare the same data-nac-action verb, so NAC.click_by_verb() cannot resolve it. SPEC.md section 3 names this a manifest error.

coded_findings.fix: Align the manifest type with data-nac-field-type on the element.
coded_findings.what: The manifest declares a field type the mounted element contradicts.

coded_findings.fix: Declare the field type in the manifest.
coded_findings.what: A field is advertised without a type, so an agent has to guess how to fill it.

coded_findings.fix: Read the message on the error; it names the argument and what it expected.
coded_findings.what: Thrown, not reported: an argument failed validation at the API boundary.

coded_findings.fix: Make the data-nac-role attribute on the element match the role declared in the manifest.
coded_findings.what: The manifest and the mounted DOM element disagree about the role of the same id.

coded_findings.fix: Use one of the roles published in contract.json, or drop the role and let the element default to action behaviour.
coded_findings.what: A manifest element declares a data-nac-role that is not in the runtime's accepted role set.

coded_findings.fix: Render the element, or remove the id from the manifest while it is not mounted.
coded_findings.what: An id the manifest advertises has no element in the DOM, so an agent that trusts the manifest will fail to operate it.

coded_findings.fix: Nothing, if the view is simply closed. If the manifest claims a permanent surface, mount it or stop declaring it.
coded_findings.what: A manifest declares an id that is not currently in the DOM.

coded_findings.fix: Namespace the ids with the plugin slug (plugin.element), or remove the declaration from the manifest that should not own it.
coded_findings.what: Two or more registered manifests declare the same nac_id, so an agent addressing it by id cannot know which element it gets.

coded_findings.fix: Rename the id to slug.element. Renaming an id breaks every caller that used the old one, so do it with the same care as changing a URL.
coded_findings.what: A declared nac_id does not start with its plugin slug followed by a dot, so it loses the namespacing that keeps two plugins from colliding.

coded_findings.fix: Declare it in the manifest, or drop the attribute if the element is not meant to be agent-addressable. Common and sometimes legitimate mid-migration, which is why it is a warning.
coded_findings.what: An element in the DOM carries a data-nac-id that no registered manifest declares, so it is reachable by name but not discoverable by an agent that reads the manifest.

coded_findings.fix: Call NAC.register() for that slug before validating it, or correct the slug.
coded_findings.what: Validation was asked for a plugin slug that was never registered.

coded_findings.fix: Provide the options resolver, or mark the field as free text.
coded_findings.what: A field advertises options and no resolver or option element produces them.

coded_findings.fix: Mount the plugin root before validating, or unregister it when the view unmounts.
coded_findings.what: The plugin is registered but no element with its data-nac-plugin root is in the DOM.

coded_findings.fix: Render every declared column in every row, or drop the column declaration.
coded_findings.what: A data table declares a column with no matching cell in a row, so cell addressing by column breaks.

coded_findings.fix: Add the date by which the exclusion is expected to be gone.
coded_findings.what: A validation exclusion carries no remediation date, so it has no expiry and becomes permanent debt.

coded_findings.fix: Remediate the subtree, or renegotiate the date deliberately.
coded_findings.what: A validation exclusion is past the remediation date it declared.

coded_findings.fix: Narrow the exclusion to the part that genuinely cannot be annotated.
coded_findings.what: An excluded subtree contains operable widgets, so the page is hiding agent-operable surface behind the exclusion.

coded_findings.fix: State the reason on the skip annotation.
coded_findings.what: A subtree is excluded from validation with no reason recorded, so the exclusion cannot be reviewed.

coded_findings.fix: Fix the findings carried on the error, or register with strict validation off while migrating.
coded_findings.what: Thrown, not reported: strict validation is on and register-time findings were raised, so the registration was refused.

coded_findings.fix: Set role to tab, or rename the id out of the reserved tab. prefix.
coded_findings.what: An id matching the reserved tab. prefix carries a role other than tab, so NAC.tab() and NAC.tab_by_label() will never resolve it.

buckets.what: A declared nac_id does not start with its plugin slug, so it loses the namespacing that keeps two plugins from colliding.
The same nac_id is declared by two or more registered plugins, so an agent addressing it by id cannot know which element it gets.
An element in the DOM carries a data-nac-id that no registered manifest declares. Common and sometimes legitimate during brownfield migration, which is why it is a warning.
Plugin slug uniqueness is broken: the same slug is mounted more than once without distinct instance ids. Reported in its own bucket so CI can gate on it separately.
A manifest declares an id that is not currently in the DOM. Expected while a view is closed; a defect when the manifest claims a permanent surface.

global_buckets.note: validate_global() reports findings as named buckets of objects, not as a flat array. Since 2.5.0 every item of every bucket carries code + severity, so section 12 promise 4 covers a real set. The code and the severity below are READ off items a fixture provokes on purpose (scripts/fixture-dom.mjs), not written here: the previous version of this generator wrote them by hand and published a null for a bucket that had carried a code since 2.5.0 (audit N-14).

stability.note: SPEC.md section 12 promise 4: finding codes are not reused for a different condition across minor versions. This catalogue is the artefact that promise is checked against: compare two published versions and a reused code is visible.
stability.since_note: since records the release that introduced a code. null means the code predates this catalogue (first published at 2.5.0-alpha.5) and its introducing release was not reconstructed from history -- it is not a claim that the code is new.

uncoded_findings.note: Kept for schema compatibility with 2.5.0-alpha.5 and earlier, where validate_global attached no code to any bucket. Empty since 2.5.0: every bucket is coded, and the codes are in global_buckets above (audit N-14, closed).
